headline: A 24% volume increase delivered without HR elevation on easy runs suggests aerobic adaptation is keeping pace with load.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your easy-run cardiac drift is moving in the right direction — HR is notably lower on comparable efforts than in the prior block, which means the volume increase has landed well without accumulating fatigue or compressing recovery. That's a meaningful signal: load went up, intensity stayed controlled, and the aerobic system absorbed it.

The 20-week running streak is worth acknowledging not as a number to protect for its own sake, but as evidence of structural consistency — the kind that compounds quietly. Paired with a strengthening strength block and high background daily activity, you're carrying genuine readiness into the coming weeks.

The June 27th effort stands out from the recent window — a substantially higher intensity and load than anything else in the cluster. Worth tracking whether that session's recovery has fully cleared, particularly if the programme now brings another quality session soon.
watch_items: Watch whether easy-run HR continues to hold at current lower levels or creeps back up under increased volume — that's the clearest real-time aerobic adaptation signal available right now.
Monitor how you respond to the next quality or threshold session given the high-load effort from late June — recovery quality after hard days is worth noting even if it doesn't change the plan.
Strength frequency has been solid but the streak is only 3 weeks — worth tracking whether it holds as running volume stays elevated.
Step data suggests high daily activity even on rest days; note whether non-training load is adding to accumulated fatigue across the week.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 155 km vs 125 km prior block (+24%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 144 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 6 runs)
